# Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric

This page describes how to enable Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric and deploy its components on Kubernetes with the Consul Helm chart.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

To install the Agentic Analytics components for cycle detection, refer to [Configure cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection/configure).

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Requirements

- Consul Enterprise 2.1 with a valid license.
- The Consul Helm chart for Consul on Kubernetes 2.1, with `connectInject.enabled` set to `true`.
- Envoy 1.38.2 or later for the AI Inference Gateway. Consul refuses to start an AI Inference Gateway with an older Envoy binary, because cross-provider failover crashes earlier Envoy versions.
- For external credential injection, Vault reachable from the terminating gateway over HTTPS, or a Kubernetes Secret as the credential source. Credential injection is not supported on OpenShift. The Helm chart fails to render when `global.openshift.enabled` is `true` and a terminating gateway enables credential injection.

### Per-feature requirements

Some features need more infrastructure after installation. Plan for it before you start.

| Feature | Additional requirements | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On-behalf-of delegation | An ACL auth method of type `oidc` with `EnableServiceDCR` set to `true`, and IBM Verify as the identity provider | [Configure OAuth clients](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/identity/configure-oauth-clients#requirements) |
| External credential injection | Credentials stored in Vault or a Kubernetes Secret, and ConfigMaps for the Credential Injection Processor and Vault Agent | [Configure external credential injection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/credential-injection/configure) |
| Auto-instrumentation | An OpenTelemetry Collector, a trace backend, an entry point that sets trace context, and applications that forward trace context | [Configure auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/configure-auto-instrumentation#requirements) |
| Cycle detection | Auto-instrumentation, a BullMQ-compatible Redis or Valkey deployment, a protection-state store, IBM Container Registry access, and a behavior policy | [Configure cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection/configure#requirements) |

## Get the component images

Each component runs from its own image. The following table lists the HashiCorp release artifact and the Helm value that sets the image.

| Component | Release artifact | Helm value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AI Inference Gateway | [`csl-inf-rt`](https://releases.hashicorp.com/csl-inf-rt/) | [`ai.inferenceGateway.image`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-ai-inferencegateway-image) |
| MCP Sidecar for AI agents, including the OBO identity processor | [`csl-mcp-sc`](https://releases.hashicorp.com/csl-mcp-sc/) | [`ai.agent.image`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-ai-agent-image) |
| External Credential Injection Processor | [`csl-au-inj`](https://releases.hashicorp.com/csl-au-inj/) | [`terminatingGateways.defaults.credentialInjection.processorImage`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-terminatinggateways-defaults-credentialinjection-processorimage) |
| Vault Agent for credential injection | Vault | [`terminatingGateways.defaults.credentialInjection.vaultAgentImage`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-terminatinggateways-defaults-credentialinjection-vaultagentimage) |

<!-- TODO: Confirm with the product owner which container registry and image names customers use for csl-inf-rt, csl-mcp-sc, and csl-au-inj. releases.hashicorp.com publishes these as platform binaries, and the Helm chart defaults use hashicorp/consul-inference-gateway and hashicorp/consul-mcp-sc. -->

Set every image value explicitly to an approved release tag or digest. The Credential Injection Processor and Vault Agent images have no default.

## Enable Agentic Runtime Fabric with Helm

1. Add the AI settings to your Helm values file. Setting `ai.enabled` to `true` enables the `consul-ai` [feature gate](/consul/docs/manage/feature-gates) on the Consul servers and installs the AI custom resource definitions.

   <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

   ```yaml
   connectInject:
     enabled: true
   ai:
     enabled: true
     inferenceGateway:
       enabled: true
       image: "<inference-gateway-image>"
     agent:
       image: "<mcp-sidecar-image>"
   ```

   </CodeBlockConfig>

   The `ai.inferenceGateway.enabled` value requires both `ai.enabled` and `connectInject.enabled`.

1. To use external credential injection, enable it on your terminating gateways. Credential injection requires `ai.enabled` to be `true`.

   <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

   ```yaml
   terminatingGateways:
     enabled: true
     defaults:
       credentialInjection:
         enabled: true
         processorImage: "<credential-injection-image>"
         vaultAgentImage: "<vault-agent-image>"
         vaultAddress: "<vault-address>"
   ```

   </CodeBlockConfig>

   For every credential injection setting, refer to [`terminatingGateways.defaults.credentialInjection`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-terminatinggateways-defaults-credentialinjection) in the Helm chart reference.

1. Install or upgrade Consul with your values file.

   ```shell-session
   $ helm upgrade --install consul hashicorp/consul --namespace consul --values values.yaml
   ```

1. Confirm that the feature gate is enabled.

   ```shell-session
   $ consul operator feature get consul-ai
   ```

## Register AI workloads

Consul applies Agentic Runtime Fabric behavior to a pod based on its `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role` annotation.

| Annotation value | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `ai-agent` | Consul injects the MCP Sidecar, which includes the OBO identity processor and the human approval server. |
| `mcp-server` | Consul registers the service with the `mcp-server` role and adds an MCP router filter to the pod's inbound Envoy listener. |
| `inference-model` | Consul registers the service with the `inference-model` role, so that AI Inference Gateways discover it as a model upstream. |

Outside Kubernetes, declare the role with the [`ai`](/consul/docs/reference/service#ai) block in the service definition. Consul rejects a service definition that contains `ai` until the `consul-ai` feature gate is enabled.
